question: A 36-year-old software professional consults a physician to discuss his concerns about small-vessel vasculitis as his mother and sister both have autoimmune small-vessel vasculitides. He has read about vasculitides and recently he came across an article which stated that an analgesic that he often uses for relief from a headache can cause small-vessel vasculitis. Due to his positive family history, he is especially concerned about his risk of developing small-vessel vasculitis. Which of the following clinical presentations is most likely to occur in this man?

options.opa: Absence of pulses in the upper extremity
